threats.description: A stolen session cookie is replayed from another device; sessions never expire, so one leak grants permanent access.
threats.control: Session lifetime capped at 12h with rotation on privilege change; cookies HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; logout revokes server-side.
threats.evidence: test: session.spec.ts asserts expiry and revocation; replaying an old cookie by hand returns 401.
threats.residualRisk: A cookie stolen inside the 12h window still works; device binding is on the roadmap.

threats.description: An unvalidated JSON body lets a client set fields the API never intended to accept, including ownership columns.
threats.control: Zod schema on every route with strict mode so unknown keys are rejected; ownership columns are server-derived, never read from the body.
threats.evidence: test: validation.spec.ts posts unknown and ownership keys and expects 400; ZAP baseline scan finds no injection.

threats.description: A destructive action cannot be attributed afterwards because no audit trail records who did what.
threats.control: Append-only audit table written in the same transaction as the mutation, carrying actor id, action, target and request id.
threats.evidence: test: audit.spec.ts asserts one row per mutation; a log query by request id reconstructs an incident end to end.
threats.residualRisk: An attacker with database write access could edit history; backups are the compensating control.

threats.description: Database credentials sit in a committed .env file, so anyone with repository or CI log access has production access.
threats.control: Secrets moved into a managed store and injected at runtime; git history scrubbed and the credential rotated; CI logs masked.
threats.evidence: evidence: gitleaks scan over full history is clean; the old credential is revoked and fails to connect.

threats.description: Missing security headers let an injected script exfiltrate page data and allow the app to be framed by another origin.
threats.control: CSP without unsafe-inline, plus HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and frame-ancestors none, set by middleware on every response.
threats.evidence: evidence: header scan grades A; a test asserts the CSP header on a sample of routes.
threats.residualRisk: CSP is report-only on two legacy pages, tracked with a removal date.

threats.description: An unauthenticated endpoint accepts unbounded payloads and unlimited requests, so one client can exhaust the process.
threats.control: Body size limit, per-IP and per-account rate limits answering 429 with Retry-After, and a request timeout on every handler.
threats.evidence: test: ratelimit.spec.ts drives the limiter past its budget and expects 429; a load run shows flat memory.
threats.residualRisk: A distributed flood still needs edge protection; documented as accepted risk.

threats.description: An object id in the path is trusted without an ownership check, so any authenticated user can read or edit another user's note.
threats.control: Every query is scoped by the authenticated user id, and authorization lives in the data layer rather than the handler so a new route cannot forget it.
threats.evidence: test: authz.spec.ts requests another user's note id and expects 404; the scoping helper has full branch coverage.

threats.description: Attachment URLs are guessable and the bucket serves them without authorization, so anyone can enumerate other users' files.
threats.control: Keys are random and server-derived; the bucket is private and reads go through short-lived presigned URLs scoped to the owner.
threats.evidence: test: storage.spec.ts asserts a direct unsigned GET is refused and a presigned URL expires.
threats.residualRisk: A leaked presigned URL is valid until it expires; TTL is 60s.
